finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /profile/avatar fetches an attacker-supplied URL server-side; the only check is a scheme prefix (https://), so the host is unrestricted and axios follows redirects to internal or metadata targets. Only the response byte length is returned, so this is blind SSRF with a size oracle, rated MEDIUM.

trace.note: typeof string check and startsWith("https://") only; scheme-only, does not restrict host
axios.get(url) dispatches the request; redirects followed by default; no maxRedirects, no post-redirect validation
Only img.data.length is returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Type check at server.js:11 does not restrict host. Scheme check at server.js:11 is scheme-only and does not close SSRF. No hostname allowlist, no IP/CIDR block, no DNS or post-resolution check, no maxRedirects:0, no per-hop re-validation. Repo has no package.json, so the axios version and redirect default are unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:11 only checks typeof === "string" and url.startsWith("https://"), which is a scheme-only check and does not restrict the host. No auth middleware is registered (server.js:5 is express.json only), no hostname allowlist, no IP/CIDR block, and no maxRedirects:0 or per-hop re-validation at server.js:14. The repo has only server.js, so there is no other guard to find.
verdict.reason: The route at server.js:9 is public, req.body.avatarUrl at server.js:10 is attacker-controlled, the only check at server.js:11 is scheme-only, and axios.get at server.js:14 follows redirects by default, so an HTTPS URL that redirects to an internal or http:// metadata address is fetched, with only the byte length returned at server.js:15. Axios's default redirect behavior is from general knowledge, not verified here since there is no package.json to pin the version.
